article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Pink Guava × Sunset Sherbert
Breeder: DEO Farms and Wizard Trees
THC Content: 24–30%
CBD Content: generally below 1%
Terpene Profile: Caryophyllene , limonene , linalool
Primary Flavors: Tropical fruit, citrus, creamy vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): Approximately 58–63 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September to early October
Indoor Yield: Moderate to above average
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Rainbow Sherbert #54 comes from the kind of pheno hunt that helped define modern California cannabis: grow a large population, examine every plant closely, and keep only the individuals whose aroma, appearance, potency, and structure rise above the rest. Often shortened to RS54 and sometimes called Studio 54, this particular selection became valued for a combination of creamy tropical fruit, tart citrus, floral sweetness, and penetrating gasoline. The flower tends to look every bit as extravagant as its nickname suggests, producing dark green buds loaded with oversized trichomes. Underneath the boutique presentation is a potent marijuana hybrid whose experience moves from euphoric mental elevation toward a deeper, noticeably calming body effect.
Genetics and Lineage

The genetic foundation begins with Pink Guava and Sunset Sherbert. Pink Guava originated within DEO Farms’ work with OZ Kush genetics, giving the family a connection to the candy-and-gas character associated with Z and OG Kush ancestry. Crossing Pink Guava into Sunset Sherbert produced DEO’s Rainbow Sherbert population. From that population came numbered selections including RS11 and RS54, with the numbers identifying individual plants chosen during the pheno hunt rather than entirely different parental crosses. Historical accounts credit DEO Farms with creating the Rainbow Sherbert line, while Wizard Trees participated in selecting and distributing elite cuts, including #54.

That distinction matters because RS54 is sometimes incorrectly described as simply “Sunset Sherbert × Pink Guava #54.” More precisely, #54 identifies the selected Rainbow Sherbert phenotype. Its siblings share the same basic genetic foundation but can express noticeably different terpene profiles, plant structures, and effects. RS11 became famous for a brighter candy-forward presentation, whereas the #54 cut developed a reputation for heavier fuel, creamy fruit, and a more relaxing finish.
Effects and Experience

The beginning can be surprisingly animated for an indica-leaning weed strain. Euphoric pressure develops around the head and eyes, often followed by an increase in sensory awareness and a brighter, more sociable mood. Conversation may become easier, music more immersive, and familiar activities more interesting. Creativity can also emerge during this stage, although the high THC content means mental clarity may disappear quickly when the dose climbs.

The transition into the second half is where RS54 shows its heavier personality. Physical tension gradually softens while the initial cerebral energy becomes dreamy and less goal-oriented. At moderate amounts, that combination can feel pleasantly balanced; heavier consumption can produce substantial body weight, appetite, slowed thinking, and a strong desire to relax. A documented commercial batch has tested near 30% THC, reinforcing its reputation as cannabis better suited to experienced consumers than beginners.
Medical Benefits

For medical marijuana patients, the attraction lies largely in the combination of mood elevation and pronounced physical calm. The earlier cerebral phase may temporarily help some consumers disengage from persistent stress or low mood, while the later body-centered effects can make muscular tension and everyday discomfort less intrusive. Consumers who dislike strains that become immediately sedating may appreciate having a more uplifting opening before the heavier relaxation develops.

Larger servings may encourage appetite and make the strain more suitable for evening use, particularly when physical relaxation is the main goal. Still, Rainbow Sherbert #54 has not been clinically proven to treat chronic pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another medical disorder. THC response is highly individual, and high-potency cannabis can actually worsen anxiety or dizziness in sensitive patients.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

RS54’s aroma moves through several distinct layers. Before grinding, the flowers can smell like tropical sherbet, guava, berries, sweet cream, and citrus peel. Breaking a bud apart exposes a heavier underside containing damp earth, floral funk, pepper, and petroleum. That contrast keeps the strain from tasting like simple fruit candy; there is enough gas and savory depth behind the sweetness to give the profile considerable weight.

Caryophyllene, limonene, and linalool have appeared prominently in tested material from this cultivar, fitting its mixture of peppery gas, bright citrus, and softer floral sweetness. On the inhale, tropical fruit and creamy vanilla often arrive first. Citrus becomes sharper through the middle, while the exhale can leave behind berry, nutty sweetness, earth, and fuel. Clone nursery descriptions similarly characterize the cut with citrus, vanilla-nut, and fuel aromas.
Growing Information

Rainbow Sherbert #54 offers more commercial potential than many exotic cannabis cuts, but it still rewards growers who prioritize environmental control. The plant develops medium stretch with relatively short internodal spacing, allowing it to build a full canopy without becoming exceptionally lanky. Mature flowers tend to be dark green, compact, and heavily coated in large trichomes. A flowering period of approximately 58–63 days is documented for the RS54 clone, putting most indoor harvests near the nine-week mark.

Topping or gentle low-stress training during vegetative growth can help spread the canopy and prevent dominant tops from monopolizing light. Once flowering is underway, selective thinning through the interior improves airflow without stripping away excessive healthy foliage. Resin production becomes especially impressive late in bloom, making humidity management important as the buds become denser. Good air movement and a controlled environment reduce the likelihood of moisture becoming trapped between tightly packed flowers.

Outdoor cultivation is best attempted where autumn remains reasonably warm and dry. Plenty of direct sun allows the plant to develop its darker coloration, resin production, and terpene intensity, while adequate root space can increase overall production substantially. Exact yield varies too much by environment to justify a universal grams-per-plant figure, although clone descriptions characterize the cultivar as an above-average producer. The final dry deserves as much attention as flowering: excessive heat or overly rapid drying can flatten the volatile guava, citrus, and creamy sherbet notes that make premium RS54 valuable.
FAQ
Is Rainbow Sherbert #54 the same as RS54?
Yes. RS54 is the shortened name for Rainbow Sherbert #54. The cultivar is also frequently called Studio 54, a nickname inspired by its striking, glamorous flower appearance.
What are the genetics of Rainbow Sherbert #54?

RS54 comes from DEO Farms’ Pink Guava × Sunset Sherbert Rainbow Sherbert breeding project. It represents phenotype #54 selected from that genetic population rather than a completely separate strain created from different parents.
Is RS54 related to RS11?

Yes. RS11 and RS54 are sibling selections from the same Rainbow Sherbert family. Both trace to Pink Guava and Sunset Sherbert, but different phenotype numbers indicate separately selected plants with their own expressions of aroma, structure, and effects.
How strong is Rainbow Sherbert #54?

It is a high-potency strain. Commercial flower commonly reaches the mid-to-upper 20% THC range, and individual tested batches have approached 30% or higher. People with low THC tolerance should begin with a small serving and allow the effects to develop before consuming more.
What does Rainbow Sherbert #54 taste like?

The dominant flavor combines guava, tropical fruit, citrus, creamy vanilla, berries, and fuel . Some expressions develop a slightly nutty or floral quality, while the exhale generally reveals more earthy gas than the sweet aroma initially suggests.
Final Thoughts on Rainbow Sherbert #54

Rainbow Sherbert #54 shows why phenotype selection matters as much as pedigree in contemporary cannabis breeding . The same family that produced RS11 also yielded a #54 expression with its own recognizable identity—darker, creamier, noticeably gassier, and capable of delivering substantial physical relaxation after an initially euphoric start. Its thick trichome coverage and high THC only add to its premium appeal.

For marijuana consumers drawn to exotic fruit profiles but unwilling to sacrifice fuel and depth, RS54 occupies an appealing middle ground. Tropical guava and citrus keep the flavor bright, vanilla-like cream smooths the edges, and an unmistakable petroleum finish prevents the experience from becoming overly sweet. Add its potent head-to-body progression and impressive resin production, and Rainbow Sherbert #54 earns its position among the standout selections of the modern Rainbow Sherbert family.
